title: Ethiopian Date and Honey Cake
community: Ethiopian Muslim communities — the Ramadan and celebration cake
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Date Cake — a dense, fragrant cake made with Medjool dates, Ethiopian honey, eggs, and spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves). The Ramadan and Eid celebration cake — the dates are cooked down into the batter, producing a naturally sweet, deeply flavoured cake.
longDesc: Ethiopian date cake is the Muslim community's celebration baked sweet — the dates (a sacred Ramadan food) blended into the batter with Ethiopian honey and a full Ethiopian spice palette produce a cake that is both sweet and deeply complex.
steps: Soak pitted dates in boiling water 10 minutes. Blend to a smooth paste.
Beat eggs with honey and oil.
Combine flour, baking soda, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and salt.
Add date paste to egg mixture. Mix well.
Fold in flour mixture. Add walnuts if using.
Test with a skewer — clean means done.
Cool 15 minutes in pan. Turn out.
chefTips: Blending dates with water produces a smooth paste that distributes evenly through the batter.
Lower temperature — dates and honey both burn at standard cake temperatures.
This cake is dense and moist — it should not be light.
commonMistakes: Expecting a light texture — date cake is intentionally dense.
cookingScience: Dates contain approximately 80% sugars (glucose and fructose) — when blended into the batter, these sugars provide exceptional moisture retention (both glucose and fructose are hygroscopic) and rapid browning. The baking soda reacts with the natural acids in the dates (tartaric and malic acid), providing leavening without milk.
storage: Room temperature 5 days. Refrigerate 2 weeks. Freeze 3 months.
reheating: Slice and warm briefly in oven.
healthBenefits: Dates provide iron, fibre, and natural sugars.
The natural sugar from dates makes added sugar minimal.
culturalNote: Ethiopian date cake is the sweet that celebrates the break of Ramadan — the date is the first food eaten at iftar (following the Prophet's tradition), and incorporating it into the Eid celebration cake connects the religious significance of the date to the joy of the feast.
